questions.q: What is the actual goal of this capstone, according to the brief?
options: Proving you can set up real Git hygiene and a real CI/CD pipeline from a blank repository, on your own
Memorizing every Git command covered in the course
Re-doing the retail-orders-analytics walkthrough exactly as shown in earlier lessons
Passing a written multiple-choice exam only
questions.explain: The capstone is meant to prove independent application of the course's practices, not repeat a guided walkthrough.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the four capstone deliverables?
options: A single commit with the message 'final version'
A working CI job that runs on every pull request against main
Deleting the .gitignore file entirely
A PowerPoint presentation with no actual repository
questions.explain: A working CI job running dbt build (or equivalent) on every PR is one of the four required deliverables.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does 'done' actually look like for the capstone?
options: The author can verbally explain what they meant to build
The repository has at least 100 commits
A stranger could clone the repository and understand the whole process just by reading .gitignore and the workflow file
All work is done directly on the main branch with no pull requests
questions.explain: The bar is that the repository itself demonstrates the practice — self-evident from its files, not from verbal explanation.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend deliberately breaking something once a CI job exists?
options: To prove the pipeline actually catches a real failure, not just that it runs successfully
Breaking things is required by GitHub's terms of service
To permanently disable the CI job afterward
It has no purpose — it's just for practice typing commands
questions.explain: A pipeline that has never failed hasn't been proven to actually catch problems — a deliberate failure is the proof it works.

questions.q: What order does this lesson recommend for building the capstone?
options: Write all the dbt models before creating the repository
Deploy job first, then figure out the rest afterward
Configure secrets before writing any code at all
Repository and .gitignore first, then a locally working dbt build, then CI (proven by a failure), then the deploy job last
questions.explain: Starting clean, proving things work locally before CI, and adding deploy last (once CI is solid) avoids shipping broken changes faster.
